claim.why_it_matters: The sub-entry 'ACCEPT statement 461' is merged onto its headword's line, so its locator reads as part of the headword. Informative index only.

verdict.reasoning: The rendered page 948 (printed 924), right column, top: 'SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 160, 162, 231, 578' is on its own line, and 'ACCEPT statement 461' sits on the next line, indented as a sub-entry. page-948.md line 62 reads 'SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 160, 162, 231, 578 ACCEPT statement 461' as a single paragraph, with no line break and no   indent. Every other sub-entry in the transcription uses the '\' break plus an   indent (for example line 87, ' SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph 232'). So the index loses its hierarchy here: 'ACCEPT statement 461' reads as part of the SPECIAL-NAMES headword's locator list, when it is really a sub-entry under it. Both sources are quoted accurately. This is a genuine structural defect in an informative index, not a normative one.
